A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same free-energy checkpoint-selection framework despite the changed title and layout. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ResNet-18/CIFAR-FS experiments, including hyperparameter sweeps and full-data and few-shot transfer accuracies in Figures 1–2 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original predictor comparisons in Table 1 and VGG-16/mini-ImageNet experiments in Figure 3 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The localized free-energy criterion, Gaussian localization, SGLD-based WBIC estimation, and checkpoint-selection procedure remain unchanged. VGG-16 is an additional experimental architecture, not a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only CIFAR-FS. v2 adds mini-ImageNet pretraining and downstream evaluation using both full 20-class classification and five-way five-shot tasks, substantially extending the empirical coverage beyond the original dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated comparisons against geometric complexity and neural collapse as predictors of downstream accuracy. v1 discusses these measures as related work but does not report this comparative evaluation; its existing training-loss curves are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds Pearson-correlation evaluation over 85 reported CIFAR-FS checkpoints and a VGG-16/mini-ImageNet protocol, including 1,000-iteration SGLD chains and 500-step full-data fine-tuning with batch size 32. These are additional experimental settings; the original CIFAR-FS settings in Appendices B.1–B.2 are retained.

E4.justification: v2 extends the learning-rate, batch-size, and momentum sensitivity analyses to VGG-16/mini-ImageNet in Figure 3. It also adds a quantitative analysis of how three pretraining measures correlate with full-data and few-shot adaptability, beyond v1's qualitative free-energy relationship.

E5.justification: v2 adds Pearson-correlation estimation across the reported 85 checkpoints. The existing five-seed repetition and error-band reporting remain unchanged; the new correlations have no reported confidence intervals or significance tests. This does not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds full-data/five-shot correlations of -0.820/-0.8901 for free energy, -0.767/-0.443 for geometric complexity, and -0.632/-0.1875 for neural collapse. Figure 3 adds mini-ImageNet transfer and training curves. The original Figures 1–2 retain the same plotted results.

T1.justification: The central bound, its proof, asymptotic formulas, and Gaussian examples are retained after renumbering and relocation. However, Appendix A changes its stated condition: v1 invokes Assumption 5.1 concerning the neighborhood minimizer, whereas v2 states only that the checkpoint is a local minimum.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains free-energy-based prediction of checkpoint adaptability. v2's introduction adds the specific comparative claim that free energy correlates more strongly with adaptability than other pretraining metrics, extending the empirical contribution without redefining the main proposal.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive applicability discussion: Remark 4.2 acknowledges parameter-scaling sensitivity, Section 5 discusses disjoint label supports and argues for broader pretraining coverage, and Section 4 discusses relating training-loss minima to theoretical test-loss minima. It also interprets the retained training-loss curves as an ineffective discriminator between checkpoints.

D1.justification: Appendices B.3 and E add checkpoint-sampling information and detailed VGG-16 training, SGLD, augmentation, and fine-tuning settings. Conversely, v1's Section 8 disclosure of JAX and Google Colab TPUs disappears. The new correlation analysis reports six learning-rate values, while the retained Appendix B.1 lists only four.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning relative to classical WBIC and BIC, citing Watanabe (2013) and Schwarz (1978), and distinguishes its fine-tuning setting from prior linear-probe studies. It adds supporting experimental citations and Kornblith et al., while removing Yamazaki et al. The broader related-work narrative remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, makes localized prose revisions, incorporates the standalone assumptions into Proposition 5.1, and moves its existing proof to Appendix C. It also replaces the reproducibility section with impact and acknowledgment sections. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format. Figure 1's panels change from side-by-side to vertically stacked, Figure 2 is enlarged and repositioned, and Table 1 and Figure 3 are added. The original plotted data are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 1 supplies previously missing comparisons with competing pretraining measures, and Figure 3 strengthens empirical support beyond CIFAR-FS/ResNet-18. These gains are qualified: the new argument that more pretraining classes addresses disjoint label supports does not establish applicability to the stated unseen-class evaluation, and the JAX/TPU disclosure is lost. Overall, the empirical case improves, while theoretical and reporting limitations remain.
